title: BlueStone posts Rs 745 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27, narrows losses by 92%
summary:
Jewellery retailer BlueStone reported a 45% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in the second quarter of financial year ending March 2027. At the same time, the company narrowed losses by 92% to Rs 4.37 crore during the quarter.

Bluestone’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 745 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 514 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.

For the first half of FY27, Bluestone’s revenue from operations increased 47.3% to Rs 1,482 crore from Rs 1,006 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Income from the sale of jewellery remained the company’s primary source of revenue. The company also recorded Rs 24 crore in income apart from revenue from operations, taking its total income to Rs 769 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 525 crore in Q2 FY26. In Q1 FY27, total income stood at Rs 752 crore.
On the expenditure front, the cost of materials remained the largest cost centre at Rs 470 crore, up 51.4% year-on-year. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 70.58 crore, while finance costs and depreciation expenses stood at Rs 58.37 crore and Rs 63.87 crore, respectively.
Overall, Bluestone’s total expenditure increased 34% to Rs 772 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 576 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, expenditure rose from Rs 745 crore in Q1 FY27.
At the bottom line, BlueStone narrowed its net loss by 91.6% to Rs 4.37 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 52 crore in Q2 FY26. The company had posted a profit of around Rs 6 crore in Q1 FY27.
The Bengaluru-based company reported a net profit of Rs 1.59 crore in H1 FY27, compared to a net loss of Rs 86.85 crore in H1 FY26.

In September 2026, BlueStone appointed CarDekho Group CEO and co-founder Amit Jain as a Non-Executive Independent Director.
At the end of the trading session, BlueStone shares closed at Rs 760.45 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 11,305 crore.

title: Ultraviolette launches X-47 Venom electric motorcycle, introduces new VX-100 platform
summary:
Bengaluru-based electric mobility startup Ultraviolette Automotive has launched the X-47 Venom electric motorcycle alongside a new 100V VX-100 platform. The motorcycle is priced at Rs 2.65 lakh under an introductory offer, with deliveries scheduled to begin in November 2026.
The X-47 Venom is the first motorcycle built on Ultraviolette’s new VX-100 architecture. The company said the platform is designed to improve performance, energy efficiency, charging speed and safety while reducing vehicle weight.
Bookings for the motorcycle open on October 22, with the introductory price applicable to the first 5,000 customers. The vehicle will be available across India through Ultraviolette’s UV Space Stations.
The X-47 Venom offers an IDC-certified range of 343 km, a peak power output of 30 kW (40 hp) and a top speed of 155 kmph. It can accelerate from 0 to 60 kmph in 2.7 seconds and from 0 to 100 kmph in 5.9 seconds. The motorcycle delivers 550 Nm of torque at the wheel and has a kerb weight of 180 kg, which is up to 20 kg lower than that of the previous-generation platform, according to the company.
The motorcycle supports 12 kW DC fast charging and comes with a 1.6 kW onboard charger. Ultraviolette claims it is the only electric two-wheeler in India to support 12 kW DC fast charging.
“The X-47 Venom brings these advances to life, combining distinctive design with deeper engineering capabilities and technology that enhances the riding experience,” said Narayan Subramaniam, CEO and co-founder of Ultraviolette.
The VX-100 platform integrates the company’s SRB-11 battery technology, UV LIGHTFURY motor and a next-generation motor control unit. Ultraviolette said the battery technology offers up to 20% higher energy density and twice the cooling performance. An optimised thermal management system is designed to dissipate heat up to 50% faster.
The battery pack also features a pyro-fuse designed to isolate the electrical circuit within microseconds when a critical fault is detected. It works alongside a battery management system that monitors cell-level voltage, temperature and current, as well as individual cell fuses.
The motorcycle features a 77 GHz rear radar system under the company’s UV Hypersense technology. The system supports blind-spot monitoring, lane-change assistance, overtake alerts and rear-collision warnings.
Other features include a seven-inch TFT touchscreen, cruise control, park assist with a rear-camera feed, Mappls-integrated navigation and connectivity through the VIOLETTE A.I. system.
Alongside the motorcycle, Ultraviolette has introduced B-MAX, a reusable rider safety vest designed to extend its safety features beyond the vehicle. The company claims the vest provides 86% force attenuation and can be reused up to five times.
Commenting on the motorcycle’s engineering, Niraj Rajmohan, CTO and co-founder of Ultraviolette, said the VX-100 architecture, battery technology, lighter motor and motor control unit had been developed as an integrated system to improve power delivery, efficiency, thermal performance and safety.
The modular VX-100 platform is also designed to support different battery capacities, vehicle configurations and power levels across Ultraviolette’s future product portfolio.
Founded in 2016 by Narayan Subramaniam and Niraj Rajmohan, Ultraviolette develops electric vehicle platforms and battery technologies. The company is backed by investors including Lingotto, TDK Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures, Zoho Corporation, TVS Motor Company, Yali Capital and Speciale Invest.
Ultraviolette said it has expanded its presence to 20 countries across Europe. The company plans to launch the X-47 Venom in Europe on November 3 at EICMA 2026 in Milan, Italy.

title: Binny Bansal-backed ShopOS launches AI creative platform Sloosh
summary:
ShopOS, a Bengaluru-based AI startup backed by Flipkart co-founder Binny Bansal’s 3STATE Ventures, has launched Sloosh.ai, an AI creative platform that generates product images, visual scenes, reels and creator-style videos from ideas, photos and videos.
The launch comes after ShopOS raised $20 million from 3STATE Ventures. The startup provides AI-powered creative production for fashion, retail and direct-to-consumer brands across India, the UAE and the US.
Sloosh uses the same image and video orchestration engine that ShopOS deploys for brand clients. The platform combines AI agents, reusable workflows and human expertise to help creators, agencies, founders and small businesses produce content across formats.
The platform offers four ways to create content: an AI chat interface, ready-made workflows called Spaces, a visual workflow builder called Spacelab, and assistance from ShopOS’s in-house creative team. Its batch mode can generate hundreds of images and videos through reusable workflows.
Sloosh also connects with AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Cursor through its Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration. The company is also launching a plugin for Adobe After Effects.
Founded by Sai Krishna V K and Ajay P V, ShopOS was built by the team behind Scapic, an AI and augmented reality commerce platform acquired by Flipkart in 2020. The founders later set up and led Flipkart Labs.
Sloosh is available globally, with new accounts receiving 20 free credits and paid plans starting at $19 per month.

title: Swiggy’s Q2 FY27 revenue rises 36% to Rs 7,571 Cr, losses narrow 16%
summary:
Foodtech and quick commerce platform Swiggy reported a 36.1% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 7,571 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 5,561 crore in Q2 FY26, while its losses narrowed 15.6% to Rs 922 crore from Rs 1,092 crore in the year-ago quarter.


For the first half of FY27, Swiggy’s operating revenue grew 36.7% year-on-year to Rs 14,383 crore from Rs 10,522 crore in H1 FY26.

Scootsy Logistics, Swiggy’s supply chain and distribution business remained its largest revenue contributor, accounting for nearly 49% of its operating revenue. Revenue from the segment rose 44.1% year-on-year to Rs 3,690 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,560 crore in the year-ago quarter.
The company’s food delivery and quick commerce businesses also posted growth during the quarter. Revenue from food delivery increased 21.6% year-on-year to Rs 2,338 crore from Rs 1,923 crore, while quick commerce revenue rose 33.3% to Rs 1,306 crore from Rs 980 crore.
The remaining operating revenue came from segments such as dine-out services and other Platforms Innovations, including Bolt and Toing.
The Bengaluru-based company also reported Rs 212 crore in other income, compared to Rs 59 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. As a result, its total income rose to Rs 7,783 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 5,620 crore in Q2 FY26.

On the expense front, Swiggy’s cost of materials surged 47% year-on-year to Rs 3,443 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,342 crore in Q2 FY26. Delivery and related charges increased 32.9% to Rs 1,895 crore, while advertising and sales promotion expenses rose 24.9% to Rs 1,298 crore. Employee benefit expenses declined 2% to Rs 676 crore.

Other expenses took the company’s total expenditure to Rs 8,703 crore in Q2 FY27, up 29.7% year-on-year.
Swiggy’s net losses decreased 15.6% year-on-year to Rs 922 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,092 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company also narrowed its losses by 25.2% to Rs 1,713 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 2,289 crore in the first half of the previous fiscal year.

The company’s shares closed at Rs 211.30 on Thursday, giving the foodtech company a market capitalisation of Rs 61,403 crore.

On the competitive front, rival Eternal (formerly Zomato) reported an operating revenue of Rs 24,138 crore in Q2 FY27, up from Rs 13,590 crore in Q2 FY26. The company also posted a profit of Rs 125 crore during the quarter, compared to Rs 65 crore in the year-ago period.

title: Exclusive: Rebel Foods grants fresh ESOPs worth Rs 170 Cr to co-founders
summary:
Cloud kitchen operator Rebel Foods, which operates brands such as Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, Oven Story Pizza and other cloud kitchen brands, has approved a fresh employee stock option (ESOP) grant worth around Rs 170 crore to its five co-founders.
The board at Rebel Foods has approved the grant of 25.36 lakh ESOPs at an exercise price of Rs 670 per option, taking the value of the fresh ESOP grant to approximately Rs 170 crore.
According to the company’s latest filing, co-founder and CEO Ankush Grover received the largest allocation of 17.09 lakh ESOPs worth Rs 114.51 crore, followed by Jaydeep Barman with 4.27 lakh options valued at Rs 28.63 crore. Piyush Kakkad, Soumyadeep Barman and Ankur Sharma received 1.34 lakh ESOPs each, worth around Rs 8.95 crore per person.
Significantly, Grover replaced Jayadeep Barman in July 2025 and has since been tasked with steering Rebel Foods toward profitability and getting the company ready for a potential public listing. A significant portion of Grover’s ESOPs appears to be linked to milestones. The firm’s financial performance has shown some progress, with revenue growing 21% year-on-year while losses narrowed 16% in FY26.
The grant comes as the cloud kitchen operator continues to grow its business while narrowing losses. According to its FY26 financial results, Rebel Foods reported a 20% increase in its operating revenue to Rs 1,951.6 crore while its losses decreased 16.3% to Rs 281.8 crore. The Mumbai-based firm has yet to report FY26 numbers.
Rebel Foods has raised nearly $803 million in funding to date, with Peak XV Partners, Coatue, Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) and Lightbox among its prominent investors.
Earlier this year, the Peak XV-backed company shut down QuickiES, its 15-minute food delivery app, within a year of launch due to high cash burn. TIt operates brands including Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, Oven Story Pizza, Sweet Truth and The Good Bowl.

title: Chapter Home raises Rs 63 Cr from Bessemer, Stride Ventures, others

Chapter Home, a home and kitchen consumer brand company, has raised Rs 63 crore through a mix of equity and debt from Bessemer Venture Partners, Stride Ventures, influencer Tanmay Bhat and a group of family offices.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen product development, enter new categories, invest in technology and brand building, and expand distribution. The company is also working on setting up its first physical retail touchpoints.
Founded in 2025 by Nitin Chugh, Akarsh Bharadwaj, Shrey Mittal, Dhiraj Jain and Dheeraj Goyal, the company is building consumer brands across categories such as bed and table linen, cookware, home décor and small kitchen appliances. 
The founders were part of the founding and leadership team at PharmEasy before starting Chapter Home.
The company uses a shared platform for sourcing, supply chain, content, technology and distribution across its brands. It also uses AI for product cataloguing, content creation, demand forecasting, product assortment, customer targeting and retention.
Chapter Home has launched home furnishings as its first category through HOKIPO, an online home furnishing brand. It plans to expand into other home and kitchen categories and sell through online marketplaces, quick commerce platforms, its direct-to-consumer channel and offline retail stores.

title: Voice AI platform Karta AI raises $3 Mn in seed round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill
summary:
Karta AI, a voice AI platform for inbound customer operations across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), has raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill Capital. Wyser VC, CDM Capital and Seedstars also participated in the round.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen the platform's end-to-end automation and multilingual capabilities, expand deployments with financial institutions, and scale its engineering and go-to-market teams, Karta AI said in a press release.
Founded in 2024 by Vijaypal Singh and Abhishek Kushwaha, Karta AI develops voice AI agents that handle inbound customer calls for banks, lenders, fintech companies and insurers. The platform integrates with enterprise systems to address customer queries and execute workflows without human intervention, unless escalation is required.
Unlike conventional voice bots that typically handle specific queries, Karta AI's platform is designed to manage multiple customer intents within a single conversation. Its predictive context engine uses past interactions, handled by both human agents and AI, to improve query resolution and decision-making.
The Bengaluru-based startup said it is live with financial institutions and handles around 2 million customer conversations a month across more than 25 languages. Its inbound servicing agent resolves around 70% of borrower queries end to end, up from 0%, across use cases such as disbursal status, account statements, foreclosure statements and property document release, the company claimed.
Over the longer term, Karta AI plans to develop reusable, industry-specific capabilities and expand into international markets.
India's agentic voice AI segment has seen growing investor interest as startups develop systems to automate customer interactions across banking, lending, fintech and insurance.
Recent fundraises in the segment include Desible.ai's Rs 32 crore seed plus round led by Prime Venture Partners, Navana.ai's Rs 40 crore Series A round led by Ronnie Screwvala, and Rezolv's $12.5 million Series A round led by Norwest.
Other players include Arrowhead, which focuses on voice AI for financial services, and Gnani.ai, which is expanding its agentic AI and multilingual voice capabilities. While some platforms focus on specific financial services workflows such as collections, underwriting and customer support, others are developing voice AI infrastructure for wider enterprise use.

title: Rural healthcare startup CureBay raises Rs 100 Cr in Pre-Series C led by IvyCap
summary:
CureBay, a rural healthcare startup, has raised around Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C funding round led by IvyCap Ventures.
The round comprises Rs 69 crore in equity from IvyCap Ventures and existing investors, along with over Rs 30 crore in debt from Trifecta Capital, Alteria Capital and VentureSoul Partners.
The proceeds will be used to expand its presence across India, including an entry into Andhra Pradesh. The company also plans to strengthen its technology and artificial intelligence capabilities to improve health screening, patient insights and clinical decision making.
Founded in 2021 by Priyadarshi Mohapatra, Shobhan Mahapatra and Sanjay Swain, CureBay operates a network of technology enabled clinics that provide healthcare services in underserved areas. Its services include doctor consultations, medicines, diagnostic tests, surgery facilitation and annual health memberships.
The company operates over 250 clinics across seven states, supported by more than 1,800 Swasthya Mitras, 530 trained clinical staff, 230 doctor partners and over 210 partner hospitals and laboratories. It has served more than 17 lakh patients and conducts over 400 health camps every month.
CureBay operates a six layer rural healthcare system that combines physical clinics, a community health worker network, a digital platform, AI powered screening, a 24/7 command centre and CureBay Kavach.
The company also works with the government on healthcare delivery initiatives and has been named the healthcare partner for Samriddhi Kendra, a Government of India initiative.
CureBay last raised $21 million in a Series B round led by Bertelsmann India Investments in May 2025. Existing investor Elevar Equity and British International Investment also participated in the round.

title: Blacksmith raises $66 Mn at $1 Bn valuation led by Sequoia
summary:
AI code testing platform Blacksmith has raised $66 million in a Series C funding round led by Sequoia Capital at a valuation of $1 billion. The round also saw participation from Premji Invest and existing investors Peak XV Partners, Google Ventures (GV) and Y Combinator.
The latest round takes Blacksmith’s total funding to $125 million. The company had raised $45 million in a Series B round led by Peak XV Partners at a valuation of $550 million, with participation from GV and Y Combinator.
Founded in 2024 by Aditya Jayaprakash, Aayush Shah and Aditya Maru, Blacksmith provides infrastructure for building and testing code. Its platform runs continuous integration (CI) workflows that allow developers to build and test software before code is merged.
The company said its annual recurring revenue (ARR) has grown 17 times since January 2026. The number of CI jobs running on its platform each week has increased from 5 million to more than 90 million during the same period.
Blacksmith said its platform runs CI jobs twice as fast and at 60% lower cost on average. More than 10,000 companies, including Ashby, Granola, Handshake and LangChain, use its platform.
The company manages nearly 10 megawatts of computing capacity across data centres in the US and Europe. It plans to expand its computing capacity at least fivefold in 2027.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its team and computing infrastructure, Blacksmith said.
The company operates in the software development infrastructure segment, where demand for code testing and validation tools is growing alongside the adoption of AI coding agents.

title: Mygate, Adonmo set to merge; Eternal to hold 4.4% stake in combined entity
summary:
Eternal, formerly Zomato, will acquire an approximately 4.4% stake in Mygate on a fully diluted basis through a share swap involving its entire holding in Adonmo, according to a regulatory filing dated October 21.
The stake in the merged Mygate entity is currently valued at Rs 156 crore. Eternal had invested Rs 112 crore in Adonmo in January 2022.
Under the transaction, Eternal will transfer 11,214 Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares and 10 equity shares held in Adonmo to Mygate. In exchange, it will receive 1,84,091 Series C1 compulsorily convertible preference shares and 164 equity shares in Mygate.
The transaction forms part of the proposed merger between Mygate and Adonmo. Once completed, other Adonmo shareholders will also become shareholders of the merged Mygate entity, while Adonmo will cease to exist as a separate entity.
Founded in 2016, Adonmo operates an ambient digital advertising platform with a cloud-connected network of screens across residential communities. 
Mygate provides technology solutions for gated residential communities, with services that include visitor management, security, accounting and community engagement for residents.
Mygate reported a 34% year-on-year increase in turnover to Rs 229 crore in FY26. The company had reported a turnover of Rs 171 crore in FY25 and Rs 96 crore in FY24, according to the filing
The proposed transaction remains subject to the execution of definitive agreements and the fulfilment of customary closing conditions.

The company claims that it has modelled more than 2.5 million people globally, including 500,000 in India, and conducted over 30,000 simulations. 
Its customers include boAt, GoodRx, Suki AI, Everkind and Concrete Software, across sectors such as healthcare, gaming and e-commerce.
Vectorial’s SAPIENS model uses socio-demographic, psychographic and behavioural data to simulate target audiences across web, mobile and AI-based applications. 
The company claims its model is 30% more accurate at predicting human behaviour than general-purpose large language models. Its simulations reproduce findings from previous user studies with over 85% accuracy.
According to the company, customers run around 600 simulations per month, equivalent to approximately 40 user studies, and conduct up to 20 times more research than before.

title: Eternal’s Dark.ai aims to offer encrypted AI chats, targets launch this year
summary:
Eternal is preparing to launch Dark.ai, an artificial intelligence platform focused on privacy and encrypted conversations. The platform is expected to launch globally this year, according to details shared about the initiative.
Dark.ai aims to address concerns around data privacy in mainstream AI assistants, where users may hesitate to discuss sensitive topics or share unpublished research due to uncertainty over how their conversations are stored and used.
The platform's introduction highlights concerns around data retention, legal requests, abuse reviews and third party logging systems. It argues that disabling model training on user data does not necessarily address these concerns.
Dark uses fine tuned frontier open weight models that run on its own infrastructure. The platform claims to offer end to end encryption, with the company stating that it cannot read users’ conversations, even if compelled to do so.
The platform also features an encrypted memory management layer that allows context to carry across sessions under the user's control. It is designed for power users, including founders, researchers, scientists, enterprises and governments, who want to keep their ideas and conversations private.
The platform's introduction also highlights how privacy concerns can limit the use of AI tools. Researchers may hesitate to share early stage ideas, while users may avoid asking sensitive health, financial or relationship questions. Dark aims to provide an environment where users can discuss such topics without fear of judgment or exposure.
Beyond privacy, the platform aims to offer answers that prioritise factual accuracy over user approval. Its models are trained to tell users what they think is the truth rather than simply please them. Benchmarks comparing their performance with other large language models (LLMs) are expected to be revealed later.
Dark is being developed for users who require privacy as well as high quality AI responses. However, details about its pricing, commercial model and the technical implementation of its encryption system remain undisclosed.
The platform is expected to launch globally this year, according to the information shared about the initiative.

title: Apple India’s revenue crosses Rs 1 lakh Cr in FY26; profit jumps 66% to Rs 5,311 Cr
summary:
Apple’s growing popularity in India, fuelled by rising demand for iPhones and other premium devices, helped the company cross the Rs 1 lakh crore revenue mark for the first time in FY26. Its net profit also surged 66% year-on-year to Rs 5,311 crore during the fiscal year.
Apple India’s revenue from operations grew 31.4% year-on-year to Rs 1,03,853 crore from Rs 79,061 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Apple India primarily generates revenue through the sale of premium consumer electronics, including iPhones, MacBooks, iPads, Apple Watches, AirPods and accessories. The company sells these products through its online and offline retail channels, alongside authorised resellers.
Product sales remained the key growth driver, with revenue from this segment rising 32.7% to Rs 99,068 crore in FY26 from Rs 74,681 crore in FY25. The segment accounted for 95.4% of total operating revenue.
Apple India also earns revenue from technical support services and maintenance contracts, including offerings such as AppleCare, which provides eligible customers with technical assistance, hardware repairs and extended service coverage.
Revenue from technical and other support services stood at Rs 4,293 crore. Income from maintenance contracts increased 26.5% to Rs 492 crore.
The iPhone maker also earned Rs 754 crore in non-operating income, primarily from interest and other sources, which lifted its total income to Rs 1,04,606 crore in FY26.
On the expense side, cost of materials remained the largest component, which rose 21.6% to Rs 78,229 crore from Rs 64,336 crore in FY25. The expense accounted for 81.3% of the total and primarily reflects the cost associated with the products sold by the company.
License fees more than doubled to Rs 10,374 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,258 crore in FY25. The expense accounted for 10.8% of total expenses and was the company’s second-largest cost head. These fees, paid to its parent company, may cover the use of royalty and other licensed rights.
Employee benefit expenses rose 13% to Rs 3,531 crore in FY26, including Rs 1,514 crore in ESOP-related expenses. Advertising and promotional expenses increased 22.6% to Rs 1,075 crore during the year, as the company continued to promote its products in the Indian market.
Depreciation and amortisation expenses stood at Rs 746 crore, while warranty claim expenses declined 16.1% to Rs 329 crore. Other overheads, including legal and professional fees, finance costs, communication expenses and administrative costs added another Rs 1,940 crore.
Notably, Apple India paid Rs 3,072 crore in taxes during FY26.

The company’s EBITDA surged 87.4% year-on-year to Rs 8,816 crore from Rs 4,704 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA margin improved to 8.49% from 5.95%, while return on capital employed (ROCE) rose to 67% from 55.6%. The expense-to-operating revenue ratio also improved to 0.93 from 0.95 during the fiscal year.
Apple India’s revenue growth outpaced expense growth in FY26, helping its net profit rise 66.2% year-on-year to Rs 5,311 crore from Rs 3,196 crore in FY25.
On the balance sheet front, Apple India’s cash and bank balances more than doubled to Rs 17,418 crore as of March 2026. Its current assets also rose 69% to Rs 38,101 crore during the same period.
Between the India profit numbers and the licensing fees, there is little doubt that India has emerged as a key market for Apple in the last three years. While the numbers may look small in the context of overall revenues of close to $450 billion expected this year from the firm globally, the fact remains that between its emergence as a key manufacturing hub, and a growth rate that is well above overall growth rate for Apple elsewhere, India is beginning to make its presence felt. The big question for Apple, and even India-watchers, is just how far the India market will grow, or the point at which the market here also slows down to single digit levels perhaps. From all accounts, that question is left for FY28 and beyond for now, as seen in the response to the latest offerings in the country. Crossing the $15 billion level in India by FY28 or earlier at a stretch will be a key milestone for the firm for now, while consumer behaviour in India in terms of replacement time or upgrades will be keenly watched as well. 
With Apple Pay also making an entry in the market, the firm is certainly pushing to round off the experience for its buyers. With a clear perception advantage on security and privacy, Apple justifies its significant premium for a  large segment of the market, even as recent price hikes might be beginning to push the limits of aspiration. It has been helped along by a rather colourless show by Samsung, which has counted on more of the same to market itself here. 
We are betting that it will not be Apple, but a competitor that finally disrupts the super-premium or Rs 1 lakh plus mobile phone market, if the situation on the hardware front normalises to allow some flexibility to smaller firms.

Other expenses, including freight, commissions, legal fees and overheads, pushed the company’s total expenditure to Rs 338 crore in FY26, up 115.3% from Rs 157 crore in FY25.

summary:
Beauty and personal care company Innovist nearly tripled its operating revenue in FY26, while its net profit rose 87% in the same period, as the business grew its sales. However, higher spending on advertising, promotions, and sales commissions added to its overall costs.
Innovist, operated by Onesto Labs, reported revenue from operations of Rs 685.7 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 246.7 crore in FY25, its consolidated financial statements sourced from the RoC show.
The company operates in the cosmetics and beauty products segment, with manufacturing facilities in India. It sells primarily through online marketplaces, its own website, and third-party offline stores.
Revenue from product sales was the primary source of operating revenue during FY26, which stood at Rs 676.3 crore against Rs 239.1 crore in FY25. Other operating revenue, which includes shipping and scrap sales, increased to Rs 9.4 crore during the last fiscal year.
The expansion also came with higher spending on customer acquisition and sales. Advertising and promotional expenses accounted for 40% of its overall cost, which rose more than 3X to Rs 262 crore in FY26 from Rs 84.2 crore in FY25. It also spent Rs 92 crore on commissions to sole selling agents, up from Rs 15 crore a year earlier.
Cost of materials consumed increased to Rs 162 crore from Rs 79 crore, while employee benefit expenses more than doubled to Rs 39 crore from Rs 19 crore.
Overall, Innovist’s total expenses increased to Rs 662 crore in FY26 from Rs 250 crore in FY25. Despite this increase, the company reported a profit before tax of Rs 30.5 crore, compared with a loss before tax of Rs 55 lakh in FY25.
The company’s tax expense rose to Rs 8.9 crore in FY26, including deferred tax expense of Rs 7.8 crore. Its net profit consequently reached Rs 21.5 crore during the year. Its total current assets stood at Rs 303 crore in FY26, including cash and bank balances of Rs 81 crore.
The financials point to a business that has expanded its sales base while remaining profitable. However, advertising and promotional expenses alone accounted for around 38% of operating revenue, making the returns on its sales and marketing investments an important metric to watch. As Innovist scales further, its ability to sustain revenue growth while improving the efficiency of customer acquisition and distribution costs will shape its profitability.

title: Gameberry posts Rs 129 Cr profit on Rs 711 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
Following 28% revenue growth in FY25, Gameberry Labs, the company behind popular mobile board games Ludo Star and Parchisi Star, continued its growth momentum in FY26, with operating revenue growing 20% to cross Rs 700 crore. Its net profit also grew over 17% during the fiscal year.
Gameberry Labs’ operating revenue grew 20.3% year-on-year to Rs 711 crore in FY26 from Rs 591 crore in FY25, as per its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2017, Gameberry Labs operates mobile board games including Ludo Star, Ludo Titan, Parchisi Star and Backgammon Friends. The company has focused on free-to-play games monetised through in-app purchases and advertising.
The company primarily earns from in-app purchases, which contributed Rs 603 crore, or nearly 85% of its operating revenue, during the fiscal year. The segment grew 20.8% from Rs 499 crore in FY25. Advertising revenue rose 17.4% to Rs 108 crore from Rs 92 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Notably, over 99% of the company’s revenue came from overseas markets, which contributed Rs 706 crore, while India accounted for only a fraction of its total revenue.
Including Rs 39 crore in other income from interest on bank deposits and net gains on the fair value of investments, Gameberry Labs’ total income rose to Rs 750 crore in FY26 from Rs 622.3 crore in FY25.
On the expense front, the company’s total expenditure rose 23.2% to Rs 578 crore in FY26 from Rs 469 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Employee benefit expenses remained Gameberry Labs’ largest expense head, which grew over 31% year-on-year to Rs 177.66 crore in FY26 from Rs 135.5 crore in FY25. This cost included Rs 7.86 crore of ESOP expenses.
Platform hosting and payment facilitation charges rose 62.6% to Rs 175 crore, which accounted for over 30% of the overall costs, while advertising expenses increased 20.4% to Rs 116.4 crore during the year.
Gameberry paid Rs 73.7 crore in FY26 under a settlement agreement with Moonfrog Labs Private Limited (MLPL) over a case previously pending before the City Civil Court in Bengaluru. The agreement included a one-time payment of Rs 32.8 crore in FY20, along with a commitment to pay a fixed percentage of its monthly net revenue until 2030.
Other expenses, including legal and professional fees, technical costs, royalty and miscellaneous costs, amounted to Rs 35 crore. This pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 578 crore in FY26, a 23% year-on-year increase.
Despite the increase in costs, Gameberry Labs’ profit after tax rose to Rs 129 crore in FY26 from Rs 110 crore in FY25, a growth of around 17%. Its EBITDA increased 8.8% to Rs 140.48 crore from Rs 129.16 crore in the previous fiscal year.

However, its EBITDA margin and ROCE contracted to 19.8% and 21.1% respectively in FY26. On a unit basis, the company spent around Rs 0.81 to earn a rupee of operating revenue, compared with Rs 0.79 in the previous fiscal year.
As of March 2026, the company’s current assets stood at Rs 487 crore, down from Rs 564 crore a year earlier. Its cash and bank balances fell sharply to Rs 12 crore from Rs 119 crore in FY25.
Overall, one would have to say Gamesberry comes out as a profitable, growing business, albeit with slowing growth, rising platform fees, and a legacy liability that scales with revenue till 2030. The ROCE decline to 21.1% is the number to watch, especially with the sharp drop in cash balances.

title: Myntra spends Rs 2,326 Cr on advertising for Rs 5,242 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
Myntra, the fashion e-commerce platform owned by Flipkart, reported a decline in operating revenue in FY26, mainly due to a 53% drop in collections from logistics services. The company also swung to a net loss of Rs 579 crore from a profit in the previous fiscal year, largely steered by restructuring costs linked to its reverse flip from Singapore to India.
Myntra’s revenue from operations fell 13.5% year-on-year to Rs 5,242.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 6,063.8 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Myntra earns revenue from marketplace, logistics, advertising and other services. Marketplace services remained its largest revenue stream and contributed 50.7% of operating revenue. Revenue from this segment rose 3% to Rs 2,657.3 crore in FY26. The segment earns fees and commissions from sellers who use Myntra’s online marketplace.
Revenue from logistics services, which includes fees for delivery and related services, declined 53.2% to Rs 1,119.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,390.5 crore in FY25. The sharp decline in this segment was the primary reason behind the fall in overall operating revenue.
Advertising services revenue grew 35.2% to Rs 1,236.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 914.5 crore a year ago and contributed 23.6% to operating revenue. The segment earns fees from brands and sellers for ads on Myntra’s platform.
Revenue from other operating services stood at Rs 229.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 178.6 crore in FY25. This category includes collection from marketing services, liabilities written back during the year and incentives from vendors.
The firm made Rs 73.3 crore from non-operating revenue, primarily from royalty income, which pushed its total revenue to Rs 5,315.8 crore in FY26.
For the e-commerce platform, advertising remained Myntra’s largest cost component at Rs 2,326.5 crore, which rose 10.5% and accounted for 41% of overall cost in FY26. Logistics charges, which cover costs related to order delivery and fulfilment, declined 16.6% to Rs 1,666.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,999.2 crore in FY25.
Employee benefit expenses rose 4% to Rs 777 crore in FY26, including Rs 235.4 crore in ESOP costs. IT expenses stood at Rs 323.8 crore, while payment gateway charges amounted to Rs 174.4 crore during the last fiscal year. Other overheads, including finance costs, legal & professional fees, and after sale services, added another Rs 455.5 crore to the total cost.
In the end, Myntra’s total expenses largely remained stable at Rs Rs 5,757.7 crore in FY26 compared to Rs 5,726 crore in FY25.
Myntra swung to a net loss of Rs 579.4 crore in FY26 from a net profit of Rs 548.5 crore in FY25. The sharp decline in logistics revenue weighed on overall revenue, while Rs 137.5 crore in deferred tax and higher advertising expenses added to the pressure on its bottom line.
Its ROCE and EBITDA margin worsened to -23.03% and -7.09%, respectively, while its EBITDA loss stood at Rs 435 crore in FY26.

On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 1.1 to earn a rupee during the fiscal year. The Bengaluru-based firm recorded cash and bank balances of Rs 21.5 crore while its current assets were worth Rs 4,941 crore in FY26.
While nowhere as bad as Cleartrip, the other Flipkart group firm whose financials we analysed today, there is little doubt that Myntra remains in a hyper competitive market where each point of growth has become a task.  Even after accounting for the fall due to the logistics line spin out, marketplace revenue grew just 3%, so the core fee engine is barely moving.
Advertising tells the contrast. Myntra spent Rs 2,326.5 crore on ads, roughly 1.9 times the Rs 1,236.4 crore it earned from selling ads. Growth in ad income (35%) is healthy, but customer acquisition remains costly.
So while the Rs 579.4 crore net loss is partly cosmetic, the fact remains that  this is a business that continues to operate well outside the rosy projections we have heard over the years on pitches and calls. Sometimes, looking at all the deals and offerings from Myntra and other online players including quick commerce ones, it seems that the whole business exists for advertising income and fees from co-branded credit cards. That might help to make up the numbers, but is definitely not a model, or a brand to be thrilled about.

title: Flipkart super.money’s revenue triples to Rs 292 Cr in FY26; losses up 78%
summary:
Flipkart-backed super.money more than tripled its operating revenue in FY26 as it expanded its UPI payments and credit marketplace business. However, the growth came at a cost, as the losses for the firm widened by 78% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Super.money's revenue from operations rose to Rs 292 crore in FY26 from Rs 89 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Super.money’s core business spans UPI payments and credit marketplace services. It facilitates digital payments and connects customers of merchant platforms with banks and NBFCs for loans, earning revenue through loan facilitation services.
The loan marketplace contributed Rs 248 crore, or nearly 85% of its operating revenue, while the remaining income came from other activities.

As a marketplace-led business, super.money’s key expense is customer acquisition and brand building. The firm spent Rs 341 crore on marketing in FY26, which accounted for around 61% of its total expenditure.
Employee benefit expenses also rose 75% to Rs 139 crore during the fiscal year. Other expenses, including marketplace, legal, telephone, postage and general overheads, pushed its total expenditure up 130% to Rs 557 crore in FY26 from Rs 242 crore in FY25.
The company’s marketing spend alone exceeded its entire operating revenue for the year. As a result, its net loss widened by 78% to Rs 264 crore in FY26 from Rs 148 crore in the previous fiscal year.
On a unit level, super.money spent Rs 1.91 to earn every rupee in FY26. Its EBITDA margin stood at -85.43% during the year. As of March 2026, the company had total current assets of Rs 136 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 63 crore.
According to NPCI data, super.money, the fifth largest UPI player by transaction volume, processed 405.14 million transactions worth Rs 19,613.29 crore in September. It accounted for 1.68% of total UPI transaction volume and 0.67% of transaction value during the month.
Beyond payments and credit, super.money has entered e-commerce with splitStore, an in-app marketplace that allows users to shop across categories and pay in zero-interest installments, with deliveries handled through Flipkart’s logistics network.
In September 2026, super.money also appointed former BharatPe chief product officer Rohan Khara to the same role as it looks to expand its offerings across payments, credit and commerce. Khara has previously held senior roles at FairMoney, Gojek and MobiKwik.
Super.money’s numbers show the cost of building a payments and credit business at scale, where customer acquisition remains central to growth. While its revenue has expanded sharply, marketing expenses exceeding operating revenue raise questions about the efficiency of its spending. Its expansion into commerce and installment-based shopping could open additional revenue streams, but the company will need to convert its growing user base into sustainable earnings. The key test will be whether scale can improve unit economics rather than deepen losses.

title: Cleartrip’s losses widen to Rs 805 Cr in FY26; spends Rs 897 Cr on discount and cashbacks
summary:
Flipkart-owned Cleartrip’s losses widened 28% year-on-year to Rs 805 crore in FY26, as the travel platform continued to spend heavily on cashbacks and discounts, which rose 47.6% to Rs 897.5 crore in the fiscal year.
Following 70% growth in FY25, Cleartrip’s net operating revenue growth slowed to 20.8% in FY26, reaching Rs 198.3 crore compared with Rs 164.1 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its annual filings with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2006, Cleartrip operates an online travel booking platform that allows users to book flights, hotels, buses and holiday packages. It earns revenue through service charges, commissions and incentives from travel partners, while offering cashbacks and discounts to attract customers.
The company’s revenue includes service charges, commissions and incentives, adjusted for cashbacks and discounts offered to customers. Service charges grew 37.5% to Rs 702.2 crore in FY26, while commission and incentives rose 52.3% to Rs 378.4 crore.
However, cashbacks and discounts increased 47.6% year-on-year to Rs 897.5 crore from Rs 608.2 crore in FY25. This continued to weigh on net revenue, which stood at Rs 198.3 crore after accounting for these customer incentives and other operating income. 
The firm also earned Rs 58 crore from other operating and non-operating sources, which took its overall income to Rs 241.2 crore during the last fiscal year.
Looking at Cleartrip’s major expenses in FY26. The Flipkart-owned company allocated the largest share of its costs to employee benefits, which rose 7.8% year-on-year to Rs 258 crore. This includes Rs 68 crore in ESOP expenses. Excluding ESOPs, its employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 190 crore.
Cleartrip’s finance costs surged 44.4% to Rs 203.4 crore, while commission and brokerage expenses increased 33.2% to Rs 171.5 crore. 
The company also spent Rs 133.8 crore on advertising, which rose 31% year-on-year, while payment gateway charges rose 39.8% to Rs 110 crore.
Additionally, Rs 334 crore was reported under miscellaneous expenses, with no further breakdown disclosed. Overall, Cleartrip’s total expenses increased 21.9% to Rs 1,045.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 858.2 crore in FY25.
Higher finance costs, payment gateway charges, commission expenses and heavy spending on cashbacks and discounts added to the pressure on Cleartrip’s bottom line. As a result, the company’s losses widened 28% year-on-year to Rs 804.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 628.8 crore in FY25, despite growth in service charges and commissions and incentives.
Cleartrip reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 640.3 crore in FY26, with an EBITDA margin of -322.9%. Its expense-to-earning ratio also increased to Rs 5.27 in FY26 from Rs 5.23 in FY25.

As of March 2026, it had current assets of Rs 743 crore, including Rs 38 crore in cash and bank balances.
The firm’s parent company, the Flipkart Group posted Rs 1.46 lakh crore revenue in FY26, while its losses stood at Rs 8,468 crore during the period.
While Cleartrip’s losses might be disproportionate to its revenue contribution to the parent firm, perhaps some of the blame lies with the parent only. From a firm that was sharply differentiated for a brilliant UI and service standards, Cleartrip today has been reduced to a ‘me too’ expected to benefit from the river of traffic coming Flipkart’s way. If there is one thing the form is known for, we are not aware of it. Subsuming it under Flipkart, even as the site exists independently for the sake of it, is not taking it anywhere. Profitable segments like Holidays require dedicated efforts, and the kind of synergies one would have expected from Flipkart don’t seem to have materialised. With the ability to launch and scale up at controlled costs seemingly lost in these giant firms, we simply cannot see how Cleartrip breaks out as it once threatened to do, albeit with heavy losses at that time as well.

title: Deconstruct revenue grows 25X in three years to Rs 165 Cr in FY26
summary:
D2C skincare brand Deconstruct grew its operating revenue 25-fold in three years to Rs 165 crore in FY26, with revenue growing 30% year-on-year. The firm continued to expand its business while keeping losses marginal, reporting a net loss of Rs 5.4 crore in the last fiscal year.
The Bengaluru-based startup’s revenue from operations grew 30% YoY to Rs 165 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 127 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded by Malini Adapureddy, Deconstruct offers products for different skin types, including sensitive ones. Its portfolio spans face, body, lip and hair care products for men and women.
Deconstruct’s growth has also been accompanied by higher spending on marketing and ops as it scales. Advertising and promotional expenses rose 72.5% to Rs 69 crore in FY26, accounting for 40% of its overall costs.
Its procurement costs increased 39.3% to Rs 39 crore during the fiscal year ended March 2026, in line with the expansion of its business. Transportation, freight, legal and other overheads also added to the burn.
Deconstruct’s total expenses grew 48.7% to Rs 174 crore in FY26 from Rs 117 crore in FY25, outpacing its revenue growth during the year.
As a result, the company reported a net loss of Rs 5.4 crore in FY26, compared to a net profit of Rs 10 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA margin stood at -5.61%, while return on capital employed (ROCE) was -13.81%. At the operating level, Deconstruct spent around Rs 1.05 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26.

Deconstruct has raised funding from investors including Kalaari Capital, DSG Consumer Partners, V3 Ventures and L’Oréal’s venture capital fund BOLD to support its growth and expansion.
Deconstruct competes with skincare brands such as Minimalist, The Derma Co, Foxtale and Dot & Key in India’s D2C skincare market.
The firm’s numbers point to a business that has scaled revenue while keeping its losses limited, despite a growth in marketing and operating expenses. However, expenses growing faster than revenue will remain a key metric to watch as the company expands. 
With advertising accounting for a significant share of its costs, the brand’s ability to convert customer acquisition into repeat purchases and sustained revenue growth will shape its path to profitability. Its next phase will depend on balancing growth with better cost efficiency.
The skincare segment has seen too many firms cross the Rs 100-150 crore milestone, only to struggle for growth, especially growth with profitability after that as investors hold out for a sale or margin improvement. Deconstruct, as far as we can tell, has not followed a significantly different route, to provide any indication for the future. Will it be acquired? Or will it cross the Rs 250 crore mark in FY27 to make it a really compelling story? Turning profitable will certainly help valuations from here on, although seeing the patchy record of acquired firms, it would be nice to see a firm break out and go it alone as well.

summary:
MakeMyTrip is in talks to acquire car and bike pooling platform Quick Ride, sources familiar with the matter told Entrackr.
“The deal is currently at the due diligence stage, with both sides examining the business and working through the details of the proposed transaction,” one of the sources said on condition of anonymity.
According to sources, the acquisition is being explored through redBus, with the transaction expected to involve a mix of cash and equity.
The potential acquisition could help MakeMyTrip expand its presence in urban mobility and strengthen its corporate commute offerings. redBus already operates rPool, a carpooling platform that connects verified working professionals travelling along similar routes and allows them to offer or find rides for daily commutes.
“Acquiring Quick Ride would help MakeMyTrip expand its presence in the carpooling segment and strengthen its commuter network,” said another source who also wished not to be named.
The timeline for the deal’s completion could not be ascertained, and the terms of the transaction may change as discussions progress.
Founded in 2015 by KNM Rao, Bengaluru based Quick Ride connects commuters travelling along similar routes for car and bike pooling. The platform also caters to corporate employees and offers daily office commute solutions.
Quick Ride has raised funding from Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV), Naspers, now part of Prosus, and Venture Highway. In 2019, the company raised Rs 100.78 crore ($14.4 million) in its Series B round from these existing investors, according to an earlier report by Inc42. It had also raised an undisclosed amount in its Series A round from the same investors.
Quick Ride’s shareholding pattern has changed significantly over the years. Naspers held a 20.81% stake in the company in 2020, while Venture Highway held 6.50%. According to regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr, Naspers’ stake now stands at around 0.10%, while Venture Highway no longer appears as a significant shareholder.
The timing and nature of these stake reductions remain unclear. It could not be ascertained whether they were part of secondary transactions or other changes in the company’s shareholding structure.
MakeMyTrip declined to comment on the proposed acquisition, while queries and multiple follow ups sent to Quick Ride’s founder did not elicit a response until the time of publication.
In February 2021, Entrackr exclusively reported that Sequoia Capital India had exited Quick Ride through a secondary transaction. The investor had backed the company in its Series A and Series B rounds. A source had told Entrackr at the time that Sequoia exited with 40% to 50% of its investment across the two rounds.

title: Leverage Edu to focus on AI, customer experience and new markets
summary:
Leverage Edu plans to increase its focus on artificial intelligence (AI), customer experience and marketing efficiency as it expands into new markets, founder Akshay Chaturvedi said.
In a post on X following Entrackr’s report on the company’s FY26 financial numbers, Chaturvedi outlined priorities including technology adoption, university partnerships, cash flow management and new go-to-market (GTM) initiatives.
He said expansion into less competitive international markets had helped the company enter new destinations. Better brand awareness and referrals had also reduced customer acquisition costs (CAC), although local players continued to hold an advantage in several regions.
The company is expanding the use of AI across its operations. Chaturvedi said its AI suite, LE-AI, had started contributing to business functions. Leverage Edu has introduced AI-based analysis after counselling sessions to help coaches improve performance and is extending its use to consumers and partners.
Chaturvedi also said higher uptake of financial services, housing, insurance and other offerings had improved customer lifetime value (LTV) and net promoter score (NPS). 
Leverage Edu’s operating revenue more than doubled to Rs 364.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 173.3 crore in FY25. Its net loss narrowed 82% to Rs 19.4 crore, while EBITDA turned positive at Rs 2 crore.
International markets contributed Rs 297 crore, or over 81% of revenue, while domestic revenue grew 60% to Rs 67.4 crore.
Founded in 2017, Leverage Edu helps students with overseas university admissions and education financing. It has raised nearly $90 million to date, including a $40 million Series C round led by Blume Ventures and DSG Consumer Partners in 2023.

Online travel aggregator ixigo has released its financial results for the second quarter of FY27, reporting a 13% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. The company also swung to a net profit of Rs 63.42 crore, steered by the sale of its stake in FreshBus and Rs 22 crore in other income.
The Gurugram-based company’s operating revenue increased 13% year-on-year to Rs 321 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 284 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange.


Train bookings remained the largest contributor to the company's operating revenue, spiking 16.4% year-on-year to Rs 149.1 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 128.1 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Bus revenue grew 23.8% to Rs 81 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 65.4 crore, whereas revenue from flight bookings declined 7.5% to Rs 82.7 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 89.4 crore. The hotel segment recorded the sharpest growth, with revenue surging to Rs 8.1 crore from Rs 1.3 crore in Q2 FY26.
Besides operational revenue, the company reported Rs 22 crore from other income, pushing its total income to Rs 343 crore in Q2 FY27.

Employee benefit expenses declined 13.2% to Rs 64.38 crore from Rs 74.18 crore, while total  increased 6% year-on-year to Rs 309.5 crore in Q2 FY27. 
Notably, on a quarterly basis, ixigo’s revenue fell 10% from Rs 357 crore in the previous quarter (Q1 FY27).
On the profitability front, ixigo reported a net profit of Rs 63.42 crore in Q2 FY27, against a loss of Rs 3.46 crore a year ago. The profit included an exceptional gain of Rs 36.6 crore from the sale of FreshBus shares and the fair value gain on its retained stake. However, profit before tax and exceptional items declined 30% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 33.5 crore from Rs 48 crore in Q1 FY27. 
Significantly, the firm’s adjusted EBITDA fell 17% year-on-year to Rs 23.58 crore, its lowest level in five quarters.
For the first half of FY27, ixigo's operating revenue grew 13% year-on-year to Rs 678 crore from Rs 600 crore in H1 FY26, with a Rs 97.6 crore profit.
Ixigo’s shares closed 4.6% higher at Rs 144.46 on Friday, valuing the online travel aggregator at a market capitalisation of Rs 6,102 crore.

title: Exclusive: Battery Smart tops up Series C round with $10 Mn
summary:
Battery-swapping startup Battery Smart has raised close to Rs 100 crore from an existing investor as it looks to expand its network for electric two- and three-wheelers. The fresh capital will support the company’s expansion plans as it continues to scale its battery-swapping network.
According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the company allotted 18,000 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 54,407 per share, aggregating to approximately Rs 98 crore from Ecosystem Integrity Fund.
The round appears to be ongoing, with the Gurugram-based company likely to raise additional capital in tranches.
In August 2026, Battery Smart had raised Rs 185.5 crore ($19.5 million) in a Series C funding round led by existing investor Rising Tide Ventures, with participation from Ecosystem Integrity Fund and Blume Ventures.
As per Entrackr’s the company is valued around Rs 4170 crore or  $440 million post money valuation. Battery Smart plans to use fresh proceeds to support business expansion, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes, the filings added.
Founded in 2020, Battery Smart operates a battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers. Its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) model allows users, particularly gig economy drivers, to swap batteries instead of bearing the high upfront cost of battery ownership.
With this round, Battery Smart has raised close to $52 million in 2026 across debt and equity, including $7.2 million in a pre-Series C round, $15 million in debt from Mirova and $19.5 million in Series C in August.
As of now, the company has raised over $221 million to date, with investors including Tiger Global, Blume Ventures and Ecosystem Integrity Fund.
As per the company's regulatory filings, Battery Smart's revenue surged 43.8% to Rs 358 crore in FY26 from Rs 249 crore in FY25, while its loss narrowed 12.8% year-on-year to Rs 23.55 crore.

title: Burma Burma parent Hunger Pangs files DRHP for Rs 150 Cr fresh issue
summary:
Hunger Pangs Limited, the operator of premium Burmese restaurant chain Burma Burma, has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO).
The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.79 crore shares by existing shareholders.
The promoters, Ankit Virendra Gupta and Chirag Narendra Chhajer, will each sell up to 60 lakh shares. Promoter group entity Bbigplas Poly will offload up to 42 lakh shares.
Among the investor shareholders, Negen Tech Opportunities Angel Fund will sell up to 64.68 lakh shares, Venture Catalysts Angel Growth Fund up to 27.72 lakh shares and L V Angel Fund up to 5.25 lakh shares. Other selling shareholders include Nisarg Ajaykumar Vakharia, Shweta Sharma and Mehul Kirit Mehta.
The company plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue to set up new Burma Burma restaurants across India and for general corporate purposes. Panthomath Capital Advisors is the sole book-running lead manager to the issue.
Hunger Pangs operates Burma Burma, a premium Pan-Asian casual dining chain built around Burmese cuisine, cultural storytelling and experiential dining. Its menu development focuses on culinary research and innovation, supported by standardised processes across its restaurant network.
According to the company’s DRHP, it had 22 restaurants, one delivery kitchen and three warehouses across nine cities as of July 31, 2026. Its restaurants had an aggregate seating capacity of 1,991 seats as of June 30, 2026, while the average bill value stood at Rs 2,400 in FY26.
Beyond its dine-in business, the company operates the Burma Burma Shop platform and is looking to expand its delivery and direct-to-consumer offerings, including ready-to-eat and other packaged food products.
On the financial front, Hunger Pangs reported a 46.56% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 156 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 106.1 crore in FY25. EBITDA rose to Rs 25.7 crore from Rs 21.4 crore during the same period, while the EBITDA margin stood at 16.51% in FY26. However, the company posted Rs 15.37 crore net loss during the year.
The company also plans to expand its restaurant footprint, explore new brands and cuisines, and strengthen customer engagement as it seeks to tap demand for differentiated dining experiences across Indian cities.
Burma Burma has raised a total of $11 million in funding, including a $4 million (Rs 38 crore) round that valued the company at Rs 500 crore in March this year.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 12- Oct 17]
summary:
This week, 28 Indian startups raised $302.85 million across 8 growth-stage deals, 21 early-stage deals, and 1 undisclosed round. The week also saw 5 key appointments, 1 departure and a fund launch.

 
In contrast, 28 startups had collectively secured about $113.35 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $220.37 million across eight deals this week, led by Tessolve Semiconductor, a Hero Electronix company, which secured $75 million from US-based Vector Line Capital.
Homegrown sports brand Boldfit raised over Rs 400 crore in a Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund, while AI agent startup RapidCanvas secured $29 million from Vertex Ventures. Bengaluru-based Scimplify raised $25 million in a strategic round led by Hitachi Ventures.
Construction robotics startup Origin raised $20 million in a round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. Meanwhile, D2C personal care brand Nat Habit is raising Rs 142.6 crore ($15 million) in a fresh round led by Trident Growth Partners.
Toothsi's parent MakeO raised Rs 90 crore from Singularity AMC, while B2B manufacturing startup CapGrid secured Rs 46.28 crore ($4.87 million) in a pre-Series B round led by Hero Enterprise Partner Ventures.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $82.48 million across 21 deals this week, led by Mesa School of Business, which raised Rs 110 crore, including around Rs 85 crore in Series A equity funding co-led by Dharana Capital and existing investor Elevation Capital. Healthtech startup Confido Health secured $12.5 million in a Series A round led by Z47.
Bengaluru-based AI gaming studio Spill Games raised $10.5 million in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital, while AI video platform Clueso secured $10 million from Dharana Capital.
AI startups Parallel Loop and Shamrock AI raised $6.6 million and $5 million, respectively, in seed rounds led by 3one4 Capital and Endiya Partners.
Meanwhile, Bengaluru-based chemical process innovation startup NuSynth Technologies raised Rs 36.5 crore (around $4 million) in a seed round co-led by Avaana Capital and Shastra VC.
Other funded startups included edtech Bower School of Entrepreneurship, advanced materials and manufacturing startup ThinkMetal, Enterprise AI startup RevRag AI, pre-owned goods marketplace Circle, among others. 
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru once again led the funding charts with 19 startup deals during the week, followed by Hyderabad and Delhi-NCR with 3 deals and 2 deals respectively. Mumbai, Shillong, Chennai and others also recorded deals.

E-commerce startups led the sectors with 7 deals, followed by AI and manufacturing startups which grabbed 5 deals and 4 deals respectively. Meanwhile healthtech, edtech, spacetech, semiconductor, robotics and others also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led the week with 12 deals, followed by pre-seed and Series A startups which grabbed 5 deals and 4 deals respectively. Series C, Series D, pre-Series B and pre-Series A recorded  a deal each.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding surged 2.7X to $302.85 million from $113.35 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $244.6 million across 24 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Nazara Technologies founder Nitish Mittersain will step down as MD to become founder and non-executive director. The company has redesignated Mithun Padam Sacheti as executive director and appointed Arun Agrawal as CFO.
Kamaldeep Singh, former CEO of DealShare, has joined Indofast Energy, a joint venture between IndianOil and SUN Mobility, as its chief executive officer.
Meanwhile, InCred Capital has appointed Abhinav Khanna as CEO of Capital Markets and Abhimanyu Kalra as managing director and co-head of equities as it expands its institutional equities business in India.
[Fund Launches]
Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A) has secured Rs 3,000 crore in subscriptions from Indian and overseas investors for its growth-stage AI and deeptech investment strategy, with Nandan Nilekani joining as an anchor investor and mentor. Led by Ashish Kumar, Debraj Banerjee and Vivek Singla, the fund plans to invest Rs 100 crore to Rs 200 crore each in 12 to 15 companies over the next two to three years.
[Financial results this week]

[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ boAt accelerates international expansion with entry into Sri Lanka and Bhutan
boAt, India’s leading audio and wearables brand, has expanded into Sri Lanka and Bhutan as part of its international growth strategy. The move follows more than 2X growth in international revenue in FY26 and adds to its presence across Southeast Asia and the GCC. The company aims to build on this momentum by taking its consumer technology products, contemporary designs and accessible pricing to more markets beyond India.
▪️ Swiggy launches multi-restaurant ordering to bring food court experience home this festive season
Swiggy has launched a Multi Restaurant Ordering feature that allows users to order food from up to five restaurants in a single transaction. The feature lets customers combine different cuisines and dishes through one checkout and payment, with a shared tracking screen for all orders. It also eliminates the need for separate checkouts and multiple platform fees, as Swiggy looks to bring the food court experience to homes this festive season.
▪️CoinSwitch Ventures rebrands as BlackLane Capital, expands global early-stage investment focus
CoinSwitch Ventures has rebranded as BlackLane Capital, an independent global early-stage investment firm that will expand beyond Web3 into fintech, enterprise infrastructure, consumer applications and digital assets. The fund plans to invest up to $5 million per startup and aims to facilitate over $100 million in funding over the next five years. Established in 2022, it has backed more than 26 startups, including Stan, Deconflict, Yousend and Uniblock.
▪️ HospitalStore launches HospitalCloud.ai to enter digital hospital infrastructure
HospitalStore, a B2B healthcare procurement and technology platform, has launched HospitalCloud.ai to expand into digital hospital infrastructure. Its portfolio includes HospitraX.ai, a hospital management platform covering OPD, IPD, pharmacy, laboratory, inventory, procurement, accounting and HRMS, and EquipTrax AI for medical equipment management. HospitraX.ai also enables hospitals, clinics and nursing homes to build websites, showcase doctors and services, and offer online appointment booking linked to hospital workflows.
▪️ FinStackk launches SalesTaxx to simplify US sales tax compliance
FinStackk has launched SalesTaxx, an end-to-end US sales tax compliance platform for businesses and accounting firms, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, where it is a Silver Partner. The platform tracks tax obligations across all US states, identifies collection deadlines, calculates applicable rates and prepares returns for filing after user approval. It also supports state registrations and closures, offers access to tax experts and integrates with accounting, e-commerce and payment platforms including QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho, Shopify, Amazon and Stripe.
[News flash this week]
▪️ Urban Company approves Rs 2,500 Cr fundraise amid rising competition in InstaHelp
Urban Company has approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 2,500 crore through equity shares and convertible securities, including a QIP, subject to shareholder approval and regulatory clearances. The fundraise could support the expansion of its InstaHelp vertical, customer acquisition and marketing as competition intensifies from rivals such as Snabbit and Pronto.
Zetwerk raises Rs 2,251 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses secured Rs 2,251 crore from anchor investors ahead of its IPO, with Capital Group’s two arms, Capital Research and Capital World, receiving around Rs 288 crore, or 12.88% of the total allocation. The anchor book also saw participation from 3P India Equity Fund, founded by veteran investor Prashant Jain, alongside global investors such as BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Nomura, Société Générale, Manulife and Prudential Assurance.
▪️ Groww’s equity derivatives revenue falls 14.3% QoQ amid CAS impact
Groww’s equity derivatives revenue declined 14.3% QoQ in Q2 FY27, largely due to SEBI’s Closing Auction System (CAS), introduced on August 3, which changed closing price calculations for eligible stocks and affected trading volumes. Despite this, its parent Billionbrains Garage Ventures reported a 54% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 725.6 crore, while revenue grew 44% to Rs 1,541 crore.
▪️Nabventures Fund II Targets Rs 30-70 Cr Investments In Agri, Rural Businesses
NABVENTURES, NABARD’s venture capital arm, plans to invest Rs 30 crore to Rs 70 crore per company through its second fund, which has raised Rs 450 crore at its first close against a Rs 1,500 crore target. The fund will back growth-stage and technology-driven businesses across agriculture and the rural economy, with a focus on productivity, sustainability and farmers’ incomes.
▪️ NPCI defers UPI MDR rollout to post Diwali
NPCI has deferred the implementation of MDR on select UPI transactions until after Diwali, postponing the October 15 rollout. Under the framework announced in September, eligible merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 will attract a 0.4% MDR, capped at Rs 300, while transactions in select sectors will face a flat Rs 5 charge. Capital market transactions will attract a 0.02% MDR, capped at Rs 300.
▪️ Qualcomm exits Shadowfax with Rs 157 Cr stake sale
Qualcomm Ventures has sold 0.98% of Shadowfax Technologies for Rs 157.28 crore through an open market transaction, following a Rs 183.85 crore stake sale in August. Across the two transactions, the investor has offloaded shares worth around Rs 341 crore. Qualcomm held a 2.26% stake in the logistics company at the end of June 2026.
▪️Nutrifresh grows revenue 51% to Rs 219 crore; targets Rs 400 crore in FY27
Agritech firm Nutrifresh reported a 51% year-on-year rise in revenue to Rs 219.3 crore in FY26 and expects to reach Rs 400 crore in FY27 as 105 acres of farms near Pune become operational. Profitable every year since its 2019 incorporation, the company also secured a Rs 90 crore first tranche from the US DFC as part of a proposed Rs 400 crore investment and signed a 1,000-acre smart agriculture MoU with the Maharashtra government.

title: Leverage Edu’s revenue jumps over 2X to Rs 364 Cr in FY26; turns EBITDA profitable
summary:
Leverage Edu, which helps Indian students secure admissions to overseas universities, more than doubled its operating revenue in FY26 as it expanded its international presence. The Delhi-based company also turned EBITDA-positive during the year, while its net losses narrowed 82% year-on-year to Rs 19 crore.
The edtech startup’s operating revenue more than doubled to Rs 364.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 173.3 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded by Akshay Chaturvedi in 2017, Leverage Edu helps students navigate the overseas education process, from university selection and admissions to education financing. The platform caters to students across India and international markets, with access to universities in the UK, US, Canada, Germany, Japan and Dubai.
Student placement services remained Leverage Edu’s largest revenue stream in FY26, contributing 77% of operating revenue as the segment grew 2.3 times year-on-year to Rs 281.8 crore, supported by the company’s expansion into new markets.
Its Fly business, launched in late 2022 to provide financial services to students going abroad, also gained traction, with revenue doubling to Rs 59.6 crore. The segment earns commissions from education loans, foreign exchange and student accommodation services.
Leverage Edu further generated Rs 21.3 crore from product sales and Rs 9.1 crore from other operating and non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 371.9 crore in FY26.
International markets contributed over 81% of Leverage Edu’s total revenue in FY26, with revenue from these markets rose 2.3X year-on-year to Rs 297 crore. India accounted for the remaining 18.5%, with revenue from the domestic market growing 60% to Rs 67.4 crore.
Commission paid to agents and other partners emerged as Leverage Edu’s largest expense in FY26, which surged 2.2X year-on-year to Rs 114 crore. These costs accounted for nearly 29% of its total expenditure and reflect the role of external partners in its student placement business. Employee benefit expenses increased 14.1% to Rs 73 crore, while subscription and membership fees surged to Rs 67 crore from Rs 11.8 crore in FY25.
On the other hand, advertising expenses declined 24.2% to Rs 45.3 crore, while the cost of materials fell 4.1% to Rs 20.75 crore. 
Cost of materials, IT, legal professional, rent, depreciation, and other overheads took its total expenditure up by 39% to 39.4% to Rs 390.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 280.4 crore in the previous fiscal year.
At the bottom line, the Blume Ventures-backed company narrowed its losses by 82% to Rs 19.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 105.7 crore in FY25. Higher commission payouts to external partners appear to have paid off, as operating revenue more than doubled during the year. Along with cost optimisation, this helped the company improve its financial performance.

Leverage Edu also turned EBITDA-positive in FY26, with an EBITDA of Rs 2 crore against a loss of Rs 83 crore in the previous fiscal year. Its EBITDA margin improved to 0.49%, while ROCE stood at -15.8%. At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.07 to generate every rupee of operating revenue. As of March 2026, it had current assets of Rs 160 crore, including Rs 31 crore in cash and bank balances.
Leverage Edu has raised nearly $90 million in funding to date, including a $40 million Series C round in July 2023 led by Blume Ventures and DSG Consumer Partners. The company is currently valued at around $300 million.
Leverage Edu’s improved financial performance comes as the company reportedly plans to go public b. According to an Inc42 report published in April 2026, the company is eyeing an IPO worth Rs 2,000-3,000 crore through a combination of a fresh issue and an offer for sale (OFS).
